cases.setup: Provide a public Python checkout, a matching traceback, and current owner bindings. No inspection has yet been executed.
checks: The public review records current anchors for load dispatch and parent initialization.
It identifies the parent-sensitive branch and correct parent semantics at every affected caller.
A confirmed diagnosis PortValue is emitted only when the supported mechanism is observed.
The diagnosis matches the declared semantic role, artifact kind, language, scope, phase, and state.
Inspection does not modify source files.
Unknown or contrary mechanism observations do not authorize repair.

cases.setup: Provide a confirmed diagnosis PortValue and resolved current owners in a public Python checkout with the supported defect.
checks: The load-analysis interface accepts explicit parent context.
Every affected caller supplies the parent established by public review.
The early load branch no longer retrieves unavailable target parent metadata.
Ordinary load dispatch retains traversal-aware parent semantics.
The builtin-sensitive incompatible-print diagnostic is retained.
Augmented assignment retains value handling followed by target handling after the early load.
A public no-crash regression for print += 1 is added.
The candidate output is unvalidated and public-validation-observed becomes stale.
No preservation or Workflow invariant key is named by invalidates.

cases.setup: Provide the unvalidated candidate and current public Oracle bindings containing instructions, argv commands, and evidence references.
checks: Bound commands are rendered before execution and match current Oracle bindings.
Public runs of print *= -1 and print += 1 do not raise the missing-parent AttributeError or an internal analyzer failure.
The added regression passes.
Relevant existing ordinary-load, assignment, and incompatible-print tests retain expected outcomes.
Public review accounts for every affected caller and preserved traversal order.
The output records actual outcomes and executed scope, including failures.
Acceptance requires all required semantic checks to be PASS, not merely an observed record.
Targeted validation does not imply whole-project or cross-project success.
Subsequent source edits require refreshed public validation.
